security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD runs as S-mode without any Smepmp awareness: it cannot read mseccfg (sticky fields prevent polling), cannot write PMP CSRs, and implicitly assumes pre-Smepmp PMP semantics where M-mode has unrestricted access to all non-locked regions. If M-mode firmware (OpenSBI) enables MML=1 and MMWP=1 with PMP entries that do not cover all of FreeBSD's physical memory as S/U-mode-accessible or Shared-Region, the kernel will trigger access faults (panic at trap.c:338) when touching unprotected regions. Additionally, the efi_exclude_sbi_pmp_cb() heuristic at machdep.c:541 assumes exactly one PMP entry protects firmware — Smepmp may use multiple entries, causing false-positive/false-negative physmem exclusion.
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD S-mode kernel has zero Smepmp (PMP Enhancements for M-mode) awareness — if firmware activates this ratified spec's M-mode lockdown/allowlist, the kernel's implicit pre-Smepmp PMP assumptions cause boot-time panics or incorrect physmem reservations

findings.finding: No mseccfg CSR definition (CSR number 0x747) exists anywhere in the FreeBSD kernel tree. PMP CSRs (CSR_PMPCFG0-3 at 0x3a0-0x3a3, CSR_PMPADDR0-15 at 0x3b0-0x3bf) are declared via DECLARE_CSR macros but never called from any .c or .S file. The kernel has zero ability to read mseccfg (a read/write register accessible only from M-mode) or write PMP CSRs. This is the root cause of total Smepmp blindness.

spec_citations.excerpt: === Machine Security Configuration (mseccfg) Register. mseccfg is a 64-bit read/write register. It exists if any extension that adds a field to mseccfg is implemented.
The Smepmp extension adds the RLB, MMWP, and the MML fields in mseccfg.

findings.finding: Three independent failure modes under Smepmp: (1) Only processes the first EFI MD entry (bool 'first' consumed after one iteration), but Smepmp may use multiple PMP entries (M-mode-only, Shared-Region, S/U-mode) to protect different physical regions — subsequent protected regions are never excluded from phys_avail, so the kernel will later access them and panic. (2) Only excludes if md_type == EFI_MD_TYPE_BS_DATA; if the first entry's type is BS_CODE, RT_CODE, CODE, or DATA, the callback returns without any exclusion despite PMP protection being active. (3) Region size clamped to min(md_pages * EFI_PAGE_SIZE, L2_SIZE) = 2MB; a TOR-based PMP entry pair can protect regions larger than 2MB, and the uncapped tail causes access faults.

spec_citations.excerpt: mseccfg.MMWP changes the default PMP policy for Machine mode when accessing memory regions that don't have a matching PMP rule. ... When set it changes the default PMP policy for M-mode ... to denied instead of ignored.

findings.finding: S-mode kernel access faults (SCAUSE_LOAD_ACCESS_FAULT=5, SCAUSE_STORE_ACCESS_FAULT=7) immediately panic with 'Memory access exception'. Under Smepmp MMWP=1 or MML=1, these are the precise trap causes when M-mode PMP denies S-mode access to physical memory — even when satp-based page table mappings are valid. The kernel cannot distinguish PMP-denied access from true hardware bus errors because it cannot read mseccfg (sticky MML/MMWP bits prevent S-mode discovery via polling per smepmp.adoc:76).

spec_citations.excerpt: Since all fields defined in mseccfg as part of this extension are locked when set (MMWP/MML) or locked when cleared (RLB), software can't poll them for determining the presence of Smepmp.

findings.finding: Page fault handler only handles PTE-based faults (scause=12,13,15). PMP access faults (scause=5,7) from Smepmp MMWP=1 blocking physical access despite valid PTEs are a different trap cause and land at trap.c:338 panic instead. The PMP layer sits below the MMU — valid PTEs do not guarantee physical access when M-mode PMP restrictions are active.

spec_citations.excerpt: mseccfg.MMWP ... changes the default PMP policy for Machine mode when accessing memory regions that don't have a matching PMP rule, to denied instead of ignored.

findings.finding: sbi_init probes SBI extensions TIME, IPI, RFNC, HSM, SRST and legacy extensions. No SBI PMP extension is defined or probed. The kernel has no SBI-mediated channel to query or influence M-mode PMP configuration. Under Smepmp, the firmware may have configured restrictive PMP entries that the kernel cannot discover or negotiate.

spec_citations.excerpt: It is expected that BootROM will set mseccfg.MMWP and/or mseccfg.MML during early boot, before jumping to the firmware, so that the firmware will be able to determine the presence of Smepmp.

findings.finding: Comment at line 596 documents pre-Smepmp assumption: 'OpenSBI uses the first PMP entry to prevent buggy supervisor software from overwriting the firmware.' Under Smepmp MML=1, pmpcfg.L semantics change from 'locked+enforced in all modes' to 'M-mode-only (L=1) vs S/U-mode-only (L=0)'. OpenSBI may configure multiple PMP entries with varying modes, and the physmem exclusion logic operates purely on EFI/FDT metadata without cross-referencing actual PMP hardware state.

spec_citations.excerpt: When mseccfg.MML is set: The meaning of pmpcfg.L changes — Instead of marking a rule as locked and enforced in all modes, it now marks a rule as M-mode-only when set and S/U-mode-only when unset. ... An M-mode-only rule is enforced on Machine mode and denied in Supervisor or User mode.

findings.finding: bhyve guest page fault handler only handles SCAUSE_STORE_GUEST_PAGE_FAULT(23), SCAUSE_FETCH_GUEST_PAGE_FAULT(20), SCAUSE_LOAD_GUEST_PAGE_FAULT(21). Any other scause — including a PMP access fault (scause=5,7) when HS-mode accesses guest physical memory restricted by M-mode Smepmp — hits panic('unknown page trap: %lu'). PMP access faults are invisible to the G-stage page fault handler and directly fatal to the hypervisor host.

Early boot assembly constructs a 1GB identity map (1:1 PA→VA) and enables satp at line 220. If M-mode firmware has set Smepmp MMWP=1 or configured PMP entries that deny S-mode access to the identity-mapped region, the sfence.vma+csrw satp sequence at lines 219-220 will activate the MMU but PMP policy will still block physical access, causing a fault in the bootstrap path before the kernel reaches C code.

smode_extensions bitmap tracks only SV_SSTC, SV_SVNAPOT, SV_SVPBMT, SV_SVINVAL, SV_SSCOFPMF. No slot for Smepmp or any PMP-related ISA extension. The kernel cannot detect Smepmp support from the ISA string or device tree, preventing conditional enabling of Smepmp-aware behavior.
findings.snippet:
u_int smode_extensions;
#define SV_SSTC    (1 << 0)
#define SV_SVNAPOT (1 << 1)
#define SV_SVPBMT  (1 << 2)
#define SV_SVINVAL (1 << 3)
#define SV_SSCOFPMF (1 << 4)
/* No Smepmp or PMP-related ISA extension slot */

findings.finding: Unconditionally excludes the lowest 2MB of physical memory for SBI firmware on FDT platforms. Under Smepmp, M-mode PMP may protect multiple non-contiguous regions or regions not aligned to the lowest 2MB boundary, causing either false-positive exclusion (excluding memory PMP does not protect) or false-negative omission (failing to exclude memory PMP does protect).

Constructs kernel page tables (Sv39/Sv48) and excludes kernel staging area via physmem_exclude_region. Assumes S-mode PTE protections are sufficient. Under Smepmp MMWP=1, PMP may deny S-mode access to kernel pages even with correct satp mappings. sfence_vma at line 960 invalidates TLB only — cannot affect PMP.

User-mode access faults deliver SIGBUS(BUS_ADRERR) instead of panicking. Without mseccfg awareness, the kernel cannot distinguish PMP-denied access from genuine bus errors, and provides no Smepmp-specific diagnostics.

Boot ordering: sbi_init() at line 579 runs before physmem exclusion at 589-619. If OpenSBI has configured Smepmp PMP entries that restrict S-mode access to physical regions, the boot-metadata-driven exclusion logic may miss them. identify_cpu(0) at line 625 runs after physmem setup — any future Smepmp ISA detection would come too late to inform physmem decisions.

efi_map_exclude_entries excludes only RT_DATA entries from phys_avail, while BS_DATA, BS_CODE, CODE, DATA, and FREE are added as available. Under Smepmp, M-mode may protect physical memory regions that EFI classifies as 'available' (e.g., BS_DATA used by firmware but PMP-locked as M-mode-only), creating a mismatch between EFI-reported availability and actual PMP-enforced accessibility.
